alerts.title: Abdominal pain: screen as suspected ADR
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening ALL patients at each encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and all suspected ADRs (mild or severe) must be recorded and reported. Patient P004 presents with new abdominal pain on TDF/3TC/DTG since March 2023. TDF can cause gastrointestinal toxicity and renal-related abdominal complaints. DTG has also been associated with gastrointestinal side effects. Evidence against drug attribution: appetite is preserved and no fever is present, suggesting a non-severe process. Non-drug causes such as gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, or functional abdominal pain should also be considered. The clinician's plan does not document ADR screening or an aDSM form.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete Drug Safety Screening checklist, evaluate abdominal pain etiology, and submit aDSM form to NDA if ADR is suspected.

alerts.title: Clinician plan lacks evaluation for abdominal pain
alerts.message: Guidelines mandate that healthcare workers screen for suspected ADRs at every encounter. The clinician's plan today only restates the symptom of abdominal pain without any diagnostic or management steps. No orders, medicine changes, or further investigations were documented. This represents a plan gap: the patient's new complaint was acknowledged but not acted upon. At minimum, the plan should include ADR screening, assessment of pain characteristics, and consideration of differential diagnoses including drug-related and non-drug-related causes.

evidence.recommended_action: Document ADR screening, characterize pain, order relevant labs or investigations, and consider symptomatic management or referral.
